label: D1 before staying on a2, early in the episode (trials < ~50)
explanation: Fires only at D1, never at GO or D2. It fires when the agent is about to choose a2 (action==2 at D1 is the agent's own upcoming choice, which it can compute) after having chosen a2 on the previous trial, i.e. an a2-stay. It fires almost only in the first ~50 trials of the episode: about 10% rate in trials 3-49, 0.3% in 50-99, none after trial ~70 and none in trials 0-1. The D1 policy logit is in a moderate a2-preferring band (choice -1.5 to -4.4 holds 90% of the mass) and the value is in a narrow mid band (7.1-7.7). It essentially never fires before a1 choices (51 of 57877 activations) or before switches. Partial because precision is only ~0.6: about 40% of early-episode a2-stay D1 steps stay silent, and adding the previous reward, the hidden good state or start_high does not separate them. Recall is ~0.97. In the examples the magnitude looks larger on D1 steps that show r0, but I did not check this systematically. The predicate uses only the agent's own upcoming choice, the previous choice and the trial index. No future random outcome.
